utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. This is a Status Conference for us to look at our Defence witnesses who are remaining and see if we can reorganise, in view of the status of health of Mr. Simo Zaric and Mr. Miroslav Tadic. As was reported this morning during the proceedings in connection with Mr. Simo Zaric's health, counsel was saying that he is supposed to have surgery performed?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour is right. He will definitely have surgical -- surgery. First of all, we thought that he would have it in the month of May, and it was the last information that we have up until today. But the recent development of his illness and information that we have just received from Mr. Zaric after he came here in the Trial Chamber, it seems that it's going to be most probably in April. I advised Mr. Zaric that if surgery is necessary, and it definitely is, he should go on surgery in the week or in these ten days when we have a trial recess, starting from April 18. But it is not solely up to him to decide whether it's going to be in April. It needs to be scheduled with a specialist and everything. So at this point, we still have not enough information to give a precise answer to the Trial Chamber as whether it's going to happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But he is on medication?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is on medication, but basically he gets painkillers. There is not any medication that can resolve the problem. He just receives painkillers, and they have their period of -- and after this period expires, he starts suffering pains, and this is the main problem that we have here in the trial. He's really willing to be present here and to follow the proceedings, but at one point he just cannot do it any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, other than the information about the last examination, when Dr. Falke said that Mr. Tadic is not able to attend trial proceedings the whole day, we do not have any new information. Mr. Tadic keeps telling me all the time that he's hoping that these proceedings will end as soon as possible. However, in my professional view, and as I told him today, and as far as his health is concerned, I told him that he should attend just half a day, until the doctor tells him otherwise. I know that this week he has therapy in the afternoons, related to his illness, and I know that regarding certain witnesses, Mr. Tadic would agree for the proceedings to go on in his absence. But I thought that in the longer term, if the proceedings are planned for the whole day, I thought that we could perhaps secure the same measures as in the case of Milan Simic, I mean organising a videolink. However, when I heard that Zaric also would be unable to attend the trial, then I gave up on that idea. So other than the report from the doctor recommending Mr. Tadic to attend only half a day of the proceedings, we don't have any other information from the doctor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Was that medical report filed?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the report which we received after Mr. Tadic stopped testifying. After that, he went through the medical examination, and then we got the report from Dr. Falke that in his condition Mr. Tadic is unable to attend the proceedings for the whole day. I have the report. I found it in my locker. It was sent to me by the registry. So I assume that it's been filed. I received this medical report about two weeks ago, so I'm not exactly sure when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. I wanted to find out how many more witnesses for -- yet to appear for Dr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the top of my head, at this moment, because I'm waiting for the translation of the additional 92 bis statements, so whether there would be certain objections from the Prosecution side. So we have to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. No. Before we --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Up to now, Your Honour, I think we have one, one witness, in accordance with the cross-examination, chief and cross-examination, and I think his name is Cedo Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That one we are aware of. How many statements are being prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mean in total?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. The ones you are waiting for, how many? How many more?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Eight. Eight, Your Honour. Among them a few -- I think two maybe are the character witnesses, so we could say, let's say, five or six are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So these statements are waiting translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Awaiting translation, yes. And then we are waiting for the position of my learned friend from the Prosecution office to say whether they want to cross-examine some of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What the Trial Chamber wanted to find out was whether it is possible to bring the witnesses in which the rulings have already been made for Rule 92 bis and continue with them for the other -- for Mr. Blagoje Simic and Miroslav Tadic, because we have to wait for Simo Zaric's viva voce witnesses to come to an end, whether it's possible to bring them and then we can proceed with them, in case the condition of Mr. Simo Zaric doesn't improve. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Miroslav Tadic's defence, as you know, already has the Trial Chamber's decision regarding five witnesses who would come under Rule 92.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partially for viva voce testimony and partially for cross-examination, and then there are another two witnesses that the Prosecution has told us about last Friday. I tried last week to see about these five witnesses that there is already a decision for. Three of them have their travel documents already, and for the two of them, such procedures have been initiated. As far as we're concerned, and with the help of the registry and the secretariat, perhaps we would need a little bit of logistics support so that they could come and testify next week. I would need to know that at the end of this week, because two of these witnesses are business people, so I have to also check back with them. I cannot just say: Come in five days. They are asking for some kind of advance notice so that they could organise their work in such a way that they would be able to come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So that in the case of these witnesses in your case, it is possible to bring them as from next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if I would be able to guarantee that right now. Perhaps I could have information about that in two days. I've only been inquiring through my investigator about their travel documents, whether they have them or not, because I know that's the longest procedure for those who don't have valid travel documents. This is something that can be taken care of fairly quickly. Perhaps I could organise for three of them to come, but I would only know about this in two to three days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The other alternative for the two accused who are unable to continue, subject to the medical report, would be to have the proceedings via videolink with the Detention Unit, in which case then we would be able to proceed for the afternoon sessions. Because the courtroom is available and the Trial Chamber was trying to see if we could continue the proceedings so that we get through the witnesses, especially the short witnesses who are coming under Rule 92 bis. This will mean breaking up Mr. Simo Zaric's sequence of witnesses and see if we can finish Dr. Blagoje Simic and Miroslav Tadic's witnesses so that we can start dealing with their closing briefs, and then while we continue with Mr. Simo Zaric, depending on his health. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like Your Honour, some clarification regarding the closing statements. Does that mean that then you would do the closing statements first and then continue the Zaric proceedings? Since this is a joint case, I don't think that we could accept to give the closing statements before the actual proceedings were completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... preparation part. No. This is a joint trial. If we continue as a joint trial, then the dates will have to be the same, because by then all the cross-examination will have been completed when we finish all the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I can perhaps, while we're on this topic - maybe it's not directly related, but it does relate to our proceedings - I would like to address the Trial Chamber about a problem that is of some concern to me, I must admit. This is actually of concern to all the Defence. This is the demographic testimony. We have asked for a decision asking the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina to act in accordance with the Trial Chamber when we receive this decision. We still haven't received any information. What I wanted to inform the Trial Chamber is as follows: Last weeks and over the last few days, in one of the cases our expert is testifying, Ms. Svetlana Radovanovic. I had the opportunity to see her on Friday and to talk to her a little bit about the method of her work, what she told me, and this is very open still, because she doesn't know what is in the data of the Prosecution's experts, and that is as follows: From the point where she would be allowed to have access to these documents, in her opinion she would need three to five working days on condition that she has the help of her computer assistant, she could make this analysis. After that, she needs at least 15 days to make her report. She needs a certain amount of time for this report to be translated into the official language, and then a certain amount of time is needed for the Prosecution to tell us what they think and whether they wish to cross-examine the expert. I see that the Trial Chamber does intend for these proceedings to go on at a certain pace, but this could prove to be a new impediment to the timely completion of this case. This is what I wanted to inform the Trial Chamber about. I don't know what we could do in this matter. Perhaps we could ask the matter to be expedited or something else. What I did propose is for our expert witness and her assistant possibly could make an oath before the Chamber about the confidentiality of the documents, and perhaps they could embark upon the actual procedure and they would act in accordance with their professional ethics in maintaining the confidentiality of the documents, since the documents are already in the possession of the Prosecution and since it has already been permitted for these documents to be looked through. I just wanted to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to this so that later we're not in the situation where we need to extend some deadlines. It is also in our interest and in the interest of our expert witness for this procedure to be completed as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: On the documents for the demographic expert, the Trial Chamber has already issued a request to the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and we're just waiting for their response. Very well. The proceedings will continue in the morning tomorrow with the witness who is already on the stand, and see how far we can go. And the Trial Chamber will request medical reports in the -- for the two accused, Mr. Tadic and Mr. Simo Zaric. And we'll also look into the possibility of having a videolink so that we can continue our proceedings, if necessary. Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There's another matter relating to witnesses which maybe we should raise at the moment. It arised from the Rule 71 depositions heard in Belgrade a month ago. There were two witnesses whose evidence we heard, of course in the Trial Chamber's absence, that the Prosecution feels should come to The Hague to continue their evidence. One of them specifically his name is Marko Tubakovic, I think. He gave evidence which in a sense could be seen as evidence against -- I think it was Mr. Zaric's witness, gave evidence which could be seen as against Dr. Blagoje Simic's interests, and the Trial Chamber's ruling, of course, in interpreting the Rules, was that Mr. Pantelic was precluded from cross-examining that particular witness. Now, when his evidence is transcribed, it will come out fairly strongly as against Dr. Blagoje Simic's interests. The Prosecution too in the 30 minutes or I think it was 40 with time banked to cross-examine that particular witness, couldn't put all matters to that witness that we wished to. Dr. Simic, of course, hasn't been able to cross-examine the witness and of course it would be in the interests of justice that this witness attend The Hague to give evidence. There was one other witness whose name just escapes me at the moment, but I can certainly advise the Chamber's legal officer later, in a similar category. The difficulty we have at the moment is that the evidence of these witnesses has not yet been transcribed. Our case manager has asked the transcription people to get on to those particular witnesses first, if possible, and that was some weeks ago. So it's a bit hard to make the application without the transcript in front of us. But I'm flagging that at the moment, as there are two possible extra witnesses the Prosecution will request the Trial Chamber proprio motu rather than attempt to call them in rebuttal because we feel that they will be more appropriately heard within the Defence case than by the Prosecution in rebuttal. But we will come to that matter as soon as we can get those particular witnesses' evidence transcribed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber is also waiting for the transcripts, to look at the objections that were raised and be able to make its rulings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. And if I may just briefly have your attention. If I understood correctly Your Honours we will proceed with witnesses that are already here in The Hague. Because here we have four witnesses. These are first witnesses from the list that Mr. Zaric listed for his Defence, and they are intended to come viva voce anyway. So these witnesses will continue -- well, start their testimony tomorrow and the day after tomorrow and this week. This is what it's going to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because -- yes. That's what I said, that we will continue with their testimony. It would have been better if we were able to sit afternoons as well, because then we would be able to conclude their testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Then we shall, after we receive a medical report from Mr. Zaric, Tadic we will decide what to do with the proceedings, whether we should bring other witnesses or break and then -- yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn now and I only wish to say that subject to the medical reports, the sequence of witnesses will be varied up to the conclusion of the trial. We shall rise.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
